An SLI counts good events over valid events and an SLO sets a target over a window with an error budget; freshness and correctness are pipeline objectives, and correctness can be measured with known-output checks.

System tables are a Databricks-hosted store of the account's operational data governed by Unity Catalog; system.access.audit records audited events, mostly per region; system.lakeflow records job and task runs with a result_state; system.query.history covers SQL warehouses and serverless compute.
Checkpoints record per-query offsets, commits and state; deleting/changing location starts fresh, and each query needs its own location.
Run-if conditions depend on upstream success, failure or completion; independent upstream work can execute in parallel.
Run if condition options, notes: when every dependency is Excluded, the dependent task is also Excluded regardless of condition; exclusion cascades.
foreachBatch supplies micro-batch output and batch identity; custom sink logic must address duplicate writes and failure handling.
Completely consume each batch DataFrame: stateful queries must consume the full batch or restart; partial consumption can fail the next batch. The example contrasts show(2) with complete consumption.
Jobs coordinates tasks and triggers, represents workflow dependencies and exposes task/run monitoring.
Repair reruns unsuccessful/dependent tasks from their beginning using current settings; the documentation explicitly says Jobs does not make tasks idempotent.
Set task values: JSON representation at most 48 KiB; set/get are Python notebook functions. Get notes discourage defaults that hide missing keys or wrong task names.

Databricks AUTO CDC (formerly APPLY CHANGES) applies a change feed to a streaming table as SCD type 1 or type 2 using declared keys, a sequencing expression and a delete condition, handles out-of-order records, expects one distinct update per key per sequencing value, does not support NULL sequencing, accepts a STRUCT to break ties, fills __START_AT and __END_AT for type 2, and can track history on a subset of columns.

In Apache Spark 4.2.0, create_auto_cdc_flow needs a target made with create_streaming_table, takes keys, a sequence_by expression and an optional delete condition, and treats the set and types of its keys as persisted state that cannot change between incremental runs without a full refresh.

A Delta change data feed row carries _change_type (insert, update_preimage, update_postimage or delete) and the _commit_version of its commit; an update produces a preimage and a postimage in the same commit, and change records expire with the table's retention.

A Databricks pipeline expectation is a record-level SQL Boolean constraint with an action: the default keeps the failing record and counts it, drop removes it before the write and counts it, and fail stops the update; Python declares them with expect, expect_or_drop and expect_or_fail; a constraint cannot query other tables.

In Spark Declarative Pipelines a flow reads from a source, applies processing logic and writes into a target dataset; a streaming table can receive one or more streaming flows and processes only new data; a materialized view is precomputed into a table and has exactly one batch flow; a temporary view lives for one pipeline execution; in Spark 4.1 a Python pipeline file declares spark = SparkSession.active(), which Spark 4.2 injects.

A running pipeline analyzes the dependencies of its datasets and flows and orders and parallelizes their execution; spark-pipelines dry-run reports syntax, analysis and graph validation errors such as cyclic dependencies without reading or writing data; dataset code is evaluated several times and must only return a DataFrame.

Databricks documents Spark Declarative Pipelines as supporting declarative SQL and Python batch and streaming pipelines, with Lakeflow pipelines extending it on Databricks through flows, streaming tables, materialized views and sinks whose dependencies the platform orchestrates; its current Python examples import pyspark.pipelines as dp, older ones import dlt.

In the Apache Spark 4.1.0 engine a materialized view is truncated and rebuilt from its query on every update while a streaming table keeps its rows and checkpoints; an update is incremental by default; a full refresh of named datasets clears their data and checkpoints and recomputes them from scratch.

pyspark.pipelines is absent at the Apache Spark v4.0.4 tag and present from v4.1.0; the 4.1.x exports are append_flow, create_streaming_table, materialized_view, table, temporary_view and create_sink; at v4.2.0 the exports add create_auto_cdc_flow, limited to SCD type 1, and the SQL grammar has no AUTO CDC statement or EXPECT constraint; 4.1.0 and 4.2.0 are listed as stable releases.

The Apache Spark 4.1.0 pipeline engine recognizes the table property pipelines.reset.allowed, default true; when it is false, a requested full refresh of that table is skipped with a log message and the table is refreshed normally instead.

A pipeline sink writes to an external destination such as Kafka through an append flow; sinks are streaming-only, defined through the Python API only and append-only, and a full refresh resets their checkpoints without cleaning results already written.
Databricks AUTO CDC FROM SNAPSHOT, available in Python, derives SCD type 1 or type 2 changes by comparing snapshots of a source, treating keys that disappear as deletes.

Databricks AUTO CDC applies a change feed to a streaming table as SCD type 1 or type 2 from declared keys, a sequencing expression and a delete condition, handles out-of-order records, expects one distinct update per key per sequencing value, does not support NULL sequencing, fills __START_AT and __END_AT for type 2, and has a Python snapshot variant.

In the Apache Spark 4.1.0 engine a materialized view is truncated and rebuilt on every update while a streaming table keeps its rows and checkpoints; updates are incremental by default, and a full refresh clears named datasets' data and checkpoints and recomputes them.

pyspark.pipelines is absent at the Apache Spark v4.0.4 tag and present from v4.1.0, whose exports include no expectation or AUTO CDC function; at v4.2.0 create_auto_cdc_flow is added and accepts only SCD type 1.

In Apache Spark 4.1.0, Spark Declarative Pipelines defines flows that read a source and write a target dataset; a streaming table takes one or more streaming flows and processes only new data; a materialized view has exactly one batch flow; the pipeline orders updates from their dependencies, and dry-run reports syntax, analysis and graph errors such as cycles without reading or writing data.
assert expression, message raises AssertionError only while __debug__ is True; the -O option sets __debug__ to False and no code is generated for assert statements.

A dict maps unique immutable keys to values, a list is an ordered mutable sequence, a tuple is immutable, and a set is an unordered collection without duplicates whose members must be hashable; list, set and dict comprehensions build a collection from an expression with for and if clauses.

csv.DictReader returns one dict per row keyed by the header; values are strings with no type conversion, so an empty cell is ''; files should be opened with newline=''; a short row is filled with restval, default None; with blocks close files even when an exception is raised.
date.fromisoformat accepts any valid ISO 8601 date format since Python 3.11, including '20260903', and accepted only YYYY-MM-DD before 3.11; an impossible day such as 2026-09-31 raises ValueError.

A Decimal built from a string keeps exactly the digits written, including trailing zeros; built from a float it converts the float's exact binary value; strings may contain underscores; an invalid string signals InvalidOperation, which is not a ValueError.

A traceback prints the call stack with the most recent call last and ends with the exception type and detail; try/except clauses handle named exception types; ValueError marks an inappropriate value, TypeError an inappropriate type and KeyError a missing mapping key; add_note (3.11+) adds text that the traceback prints.

A requirement can carry --hash=sha256:… values; hash-checking mode, forced by --require-hashes, requires every requirement to be pinned with == and to have a hash, and verifies downloaded archives against them.

int() accepts surrounding whitespace, a sign and underscores between digits in strings, truncates floats toward zero, accepts bool because bool subclasses int, raises ValueError for text such as '12.0' or 'twelve' and TypeError for None.

json.load maps JSON null to None, true to True, integer numbers to int and real numbers to float, and an absent key is simply absent; parse_float can build Decimal instead; invalid JSON raises JSONDecodeError, a ValueError; json.dumps raises TypeError for Decimal or date unless a default function is given.

logging.getLogger(name) returns one shared logger per name in a dotted hierarchy; messages are format strings merged with arguments; basicConfig configures the root logger; libraries should add no handler other than NullHandler, leaving configuration to the application; unconfigured WARNING events go to stderr through a last-resort handler.
Importing a module runs its top-level statements once per interpreter session; run as a script its __name__ is '__main__', so a guarded block runs only then and not when a test imports it.

None, False, numeric zero and empty strings and collections are all false in a truth test; None is compared with 'is'; None == None is True, unlike SQL NULL comparisons, and ordering None against a number is not defined.
Since Python 3.11 an exception's add_note(note) appends a string that the standard traceback prints after the exception; raise ... from error chains a new exception to its cause.

json.load and json.loads accept parse_float, called with the string of every JSON real number; passing decimal.Decimal builds Decimal values from the original text, while integers still use parse_int.
csv.DictReader fills the missing fields of a short non-blank row with restval, default None, and collects extra fields of a long row in a list under restkey, default None.

Every value has a type; objects of different types other than numeric types never compare equal, so '12' == 12 is False; bool is a subclass of int, so True is accepted wherever an int is and isinstance(True, int) is True while type(True) is int is False; floats are binary approximations, so 0.1 + 0.2 prints 0.30000000000000004.
The runtime does not enforce function and variable annotations; they serve type checkers, IDEs and linters; X | Y union syntax in annotations is available from Python 3.10.
unittest tests are TestCase methods named test…; assertEqual, assertIs, assertRaises and assertLogs check results, exceptions and log lines, and assertLogs reports lines as LEVEL:logger:message.

python -m venv creates an environment with its own site-packages on top of a base interpreter and sys.prefix differs from sys.base_prefix inside it; python -m pip freeze > requirements.txt records installed versions for python -m pip install -r; pinning uses ==, and freeze pins transitive dependencies too.

A dict maps unique hashable keys to values, a list is ordered and mutable, a tuple is immutable, a set holds distinct hashable members, and comprehensions build these collections from for and if clauses.

int() accepts whitespace, a sign and underscores, truncates floats and accepts bool; Decimal built from a float converts its exact binary value and an invalid string signals InvalidOperation; date.fromisoformat accepts forms such as 20260903 only since Python 3.11.
python -m venv creates an isolated environment with its own site-packages; python -m pip freeze > requirements.txt records exact versions, and pinning uses ==.

A traceback lists the most recent call last and ends with the exception type and message; ValueError, TypeError and KeyError mark a bad value, a bad type and a missing key; assert statements generate no code under python -O.
The runtime does not enforce type annotations; X | Y union syntax is available from Python 3.10.
logging.getLogger(name) returns one shared logger per dotted name; basicConfig configures the root logger; libraries should add no handler other than NullHandler.
Importing a module runs its top level once per session; a module run as a script has __name__ '__main__', so a guarded block runs only then.
csv.DictReader returns dicts of strings keyed by the header; json.load maps null to None, true to True and numbers to int or float; with blocks close files even when an exception is raised.
unittest tests are TestCase methods named test… that use assertion methods such as assertEqual and assertLogs; assertLogs reports LEVEL:logger:message lines.

Python compares by type and never casts text to a number in a comparison, so '12' == 12 is False; bool subclasses int; floats are binary approximations; None, False, 0 and '' are false in a truth test.

An AI Search index is either Delta Sync, kept in step with a source Delta table by a TRIGGERED pipeline (one refresh with the data available when it starts) or a CONTINUOUS one (processes new data as it arrives), with embeddings computed from a source column by a model endpoint or supplied in a vector column, or Direct Access, whose rows and vectors are written through the API; an index is named by a Unity Catalog table name and hosted on a STANDARD or STORAGE_OPTIMIZED endpoint, where the SDK notes that a storage-optimized endpoint accepts only a TRIGGERED pipeline.

Databricks AI Search is the current name of the managed vector and keyword search service previously called Databricks Vector Search; the databricks-ai-search client replaces the deprecated databricks-vectorsearch package, and the SDK's AiSearchAPI replaces the legacy VectorSearchEndpoints API.
The AI Search overview describes an index built from source data and metadata, embedding similarity, hybrid keyword search and filtering.

ai_parse_document parses PDF, DOCX, DOC, PPTX, PPT, JPG, JPEG, PNG and TIFF files given as a Unity Catalog volume path into a document of pages and elements, and reports individual pages that failed in a per-page error list while the request succeeds.

AI Search queries accept query_type ANN (the default), HYBRID or FULL_TEXT, filters, a score threshold and an optional reranker over named columns; the client documents that a score threshold is applied before reranking.

MLflow 3.16.1 defines recall at k as unique relevant retrieved ids in the top k divided by the number of ground-truth ids (a metric deprecated since 3.4.0 in favour of GenAI evaluation), and provides judge-based scorers for retrieval groundedness, chunk relevance and context sufficiency.

An AI Search index subtype is HYBRID (vector embeddings for similarity search and hybrid search, the default) or FULL_TEXT (keyword search without embeddings); the client marks the subtype parameter as beta and FULL_TEXT as supported only on STORAGE_OPTIMIZED endpoints.

scikit-learn's TfidfVectorizer lower-cases text, keeps tokens of two or more alphanumeric characters, weights each token by count times idf(t) = ln((1 + n) / (1 + df(t))) + 1 and scales each row to unit l2 length, so cosine similarity is a dot product.

Databricks AI Search, formerly Vector Search, is a managed vector and keyword search service whose queries accept query_type ANN (default), HYBRID or FULL_TEXT, filters, a score threshold applied before reranking, and an optional reranker.
ai_parse_document parses PDF, DOCX, DOC, PPTX, PPT, JPG, JPEG, PNG and TIFF files from a Unity Catalog volume path into pages and elements and lists pages that failed.
MLflow defines recall at k over labelled relevant ids and provides judge-based scorers for retrieval groundedness, relevance and sufficiency.

An AI Search Delta Sync index follows a source Delta table with a TRIGGERED pipeline (one refresh with the data available at its start) or a CONTINUOUS one; a Direct Access index is written through the API; embeddings are computed from a source column by a model endpoint or supplied as vectors.
TfidfVectorizer's defaults lower-case text, keep tokens of two or more alphanumeric characters, weight count × (ln((1 + n)/(1 + df)) + 1) and normalise rows to unit length.
ai_query can call traditional and fully custom ML models from SQL when they are deployed on Model Serving endpoints.
A registered version, addressed by name and alias, scores a Spark DataFrame through a pyfunc Spark UDF; AI Functions including ai_query can score from SQL inside pipelines and jobs.

With scale to zero the concurrency floor becomes zero after 30 minutes of inactivity; the first request afterwards waits for a cold start that usually takes ten to twenty seconds and sometimes minutes, with no SLA, so it is not for workloads that need guaranteed response times.
The debugging guide and the build and service logs are the documented first places to read when a deployment fails to build or start.

Data profiling is part of data quality monitoring, which runs on serverless compute billed under a data quality monitoring billing product and does not modify the monitored tables; the older quality_monitors API page is marked deprecated.

An endpoint holds served entities with a workload size, a scale-to-zero flag and a traffic configuration; workload sizes map to provisioned-concurrency ranges (Small 4, Medium 8 to 16, Large 16 to 64 as read at search time), one unit serves one request at a time, and the page estimates required concurrency as queries per second times model execution time.

Endpoint health metrics report latency, request rate, error rate, CPU and memory; the metrics export API delivers latency and queue-time histograms, 4xx and 5xx counts and provisioned concurrency to Prometheus or Datadog; service and build logs support debugging.

Inference tables log each request and response into a Unity Catalog Delta table, joinable with labels for evaluation and retraining; an AI Gateway-enabled variant, which Databricks recommends, and a legacy variant are documented with different columns, and rows can take up to an hour to appear.

For a model logged with the feature engineering client, the endpoint uses the keys in a request to look up precomputed features from a Databricks Online Feature Store, which is powered by Lakebase, or from a third-party online store.
One endpoint can serve at most ten served entities with a traffic percentage each, changed by a configuration update, so a release and a rollback are traffic changes.

Data profiling (formerly Lakehouse Monitoring) writes a profile metrics table and a drift metrics table per monitor; the InferenceLog profile adds performance metrics when prediction and label columns are present, and drift is computed against a baseline table or consecutive windows.
Requests carry a JSON-serialized pandas DataFrame under dataframe_split or dataframe_records, or tensors under instances or inputs, and the response returns predictions.

Route optimization lowers overhead latency and raises supported queries per second; it is set when an endpoint is created, and a route-optimized endpoint is queried at its own URL with OAuth tokens rather than personal access tokens.

A model logged with the feature engineering client keeps references to its features; in batch, score_batch joins point-in-time correct feature values from the offline store to rows that carry only the keys, then scores them.

Open-source MLflow's scoring server accepts exactly one of the four input keys, parses the JSON body with the signature's types before prediction, and then enforces the signature, so a value the parser can cast is accepted and one it cannot is refused as a bad request.
Model Serving deploys MLflow models as managed REST endpoints and supports real-time and batch inference for custom models registered in Unity Catalog.

MLflow schema enforcement validates inputs against the signature before the model runs: missing required inputs raise, undeclared inputs are ignored, columns match by name, and column-based signatures accept only lossless type conversions, such as int to double but not long to double.

A registered model can score a Spark DataFrame through mlflow.pyfunc.spark_udf, loaded by name and alias from Unity Catalog; AI Functions such as ai_query can call served models from SQL, including traditional ML models deployed on Model Serving endpoints.

An endpoint holds served entities with a workload size mapped to a provisioned-concurrency range (Small 4, Medium 8 to 16, Large 16 to 64 as read at search time), one unit of concurrency serves one request at a time, required concurrency is estimated as queries per second times model execution time, and scale to zero lets the lower bound reach zero after 30 minutes of inactivity, followed by a cold start of usually ten to twenty seconds and sometimes minutes with no SLA.

Endpoint health metrics report latency, request rate, error rate, CPU and memory and can be exported to Prometheus and Datadog; service and build logs support deployment debugging; data profiling covers model performance and drift.
Inference tables log each request and response as rows of a Delta table in Unity Catalog, which can be joined with labels to evaluate and retrain.
For a model logged with the feature engineering client, the serving endpoint uses the entity keys in a request to look up precomputed features from an online store at inference time.
One endpoint can serve several models or versions with a configured traffic percentage per served entity, so a release and a rollback are traffic changes.

Data profiling (formerly Lakehouse Monitoring) computes profile and drift metric tables for a monitored table; the InferenceLog profile adds model performance metrics when prediction and label columns are provided and drift when a baseline table or consecutive windows exist.
Requests carry a JSON-serialized pandas DataFrame under dataframe_split or dataframe_records, or tensors under instances or inputs, and the response returns predictions.

A model logged with the feature engineering client keeps references to its features, and FeatureEngineeringClient.score_batch joins point-in-time correct feature values from the offline store to rows that carry only the keys before scoring.

Open-source MLflow's scoring server accepts exactly one of the four input keys, parses the JSON body with the signature's types before prediction, then enforces the signature, so a castable value is accepted and an uncastable one is refused as a bad request.
Model Serving deploys MLflow models as REST endpoints without managed infrastructure on the customer's side and supports real-time and batch inference for custom models.

MLflow schema enforcement validates inputs against the model signature before the model runs: missing required inputs raise, undeclared inputs are ignored, and only lossless type conversions are accepted for column-based signatures, such as int to double but not long to double.

The protocol defines URL-based access, where the server lists pre-signed file URLs, and directory-based access, where it issues temporary read-only cloud credentials for the table root with an expiration time; table metadata lists supported accessModes, and a client supporting only URLs must fail on a directory-only table.

Recipients can read a shared table's change data feed between versions or timestamps, with _change_type, _commit_version and _commit_timestamp columns, when the provider enables change data feed on the shared object; start_version bounds how far back they may go; the Python connector exposes load_table_changes_as_pandas.

A Databricks clean room uses Delta Sharing and serverless compute so parties work together without direct access to each other's data; collaborators are identified by Unity Catalog global metastore identifiers; assets are tables, views, volumes, foreign tables, notebooks and JAR analyses; notebooks carry APPROVED, PENDING or REJECTED reviews and a list of collaborators allowed to run them; results go to an output catalog; the owner must keep privileges on assets; a deleted clean room remains in other collaborators' metastores in a deleted state.

Lakehouse Federation uses a Unity Catalog connection holding an external source's options and credentials and a foreign catalog created from that connection; query federation pushes work to the remote database while catalog federation reads external tables from object storage with Databricks compute; the overview describes both as read-only; connection types in the API include PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Snowflake, Redshift, BigQuery, Oracle, Teradata, Hive metastore and AWS Glue, governed by CREATE CONNECTION, USE CONNECTION and CREATE FOREIGN CATALOG.

Iceberg REST catalog clients call /v1/config, then load a table to receive its metadata location and configuration, and may request vended credentials or remote signing for storage access; the open-source Unity Catalog states compatibility with the Iceberg REST catalog API and the Hive metastore API.

Lakeflow Connect provides managed ingestion connectors in categories including change-data-capture database ingestion, files, streaming and query-based ingestion, with service models and source support that differ by connector.

Databricks' current documentation titles its sharing overview 'What is OpenSharing?', and the historical delta-sharing documentation URL leads there; the open protocol specification is titled Delta Sharing Protocol; connectors read shares through the deltaSharing Spark format and the delta_sharing Python package; the Databricks API names the resources shares, recipients and providers and still describes a delta sharing authentication type.

Recipient federation policies let non-Databricks recipients authenticate with short-lived OIDC tokens issued by their own identity provider, validated by claims set on the recipient, for user-to-machine and machine-to-machine flows, without static credentials.

A recipient's profile file contains shareCredentialsVersion, the sharing server endpoint, a bearer token and an optional expirationTime, and a token without expirationTime can be seen as never expiring; connectors address a shared table as the profile path followed by '#' and share, schema and table names.

A shared object's partition value can refer to a recipient property key instead of a literal value, and recipients carry key-value properties, so one shared table can expose different partitions to different recipients.

In the Delta Sharing protocol every REST call carries a bearer token; a read returns the table's files as HTTPS URLs that the client downloads directly, each optionally with an expiration timestamp, or temporary read-only credentials for the table directory; predicate and limit hints are best effort and the client must apply them; older versions or timestamps are served only with history sharing; clients may cache files by id and check the table version to detect staleness; the delta response format enables reading tables with advanced reader features, and a client that did not request it must fail if the server answers in it.

In Lakehouse Federation some predicates push down to the source while others remain local; EXPLAIN FORMATTED exposes the remote query, with an adaptive-execution caveat; JDBC fetchSize controls rows per batch, not parallelism.

Databricks-to-Databricks recipients are created from the recipient's sharing identifier (cloud:region:metastore-uuid) and exchange no token; open-sharing recipients download a credential file once from an activation link or authenticate with OIDC federation; recipients can carry an IP access list and a token expiry; rotate_token can only shorten the existing token's expiry and 0 expires it at once; creating a recipient needs CREATE_RECIPIENT.

A share is a container of existing metastore objects, optionally under aliases; object types in the API include tables, views, materialized views, streaming tables, foreign tables, volumes, models, functions and notebook files; the share owner must keep SELECT on each shared table indefinitely and a group owner is advised; history sharing is disabled unless enabled; start_version sets the lowest queryable version; granting needs USE_SHARE and SET_SHARE_PERMISSION or ownership, and revoking a recipient needs no additional privilege; a recipient's Delta Sharing catalog is created from a provider name and share name.

UniForm lets Iceberg clients read a Delta table from the same Parquet files by generating Iceberg metadata asynchronously after each Delta commit, possibly bundling commits; converted_delta_version records the Delta version reflected; it is enabled by delta.enableIcebergCompatV2 and delta.universalFormat.enabledFormats, requires column mapping and irreversible protocol upgrades, is read-only for Iceberg clients, and in open-source Delta does not work with deletion vectors.

Unity Catalog's temporary table credentials are short-lived, downscoped storage credentials (STS on AWS, SAS on Azure, OAuth on Google Cloud); issuing them requires a metastore admin to enable the external access flag, off by default, and the catalog owner to grant EXTERNAL USE SCHEMA, which schema ownership and ALL PRIVILEGES do not include.

A Databricks clean room uses Delta Sharing and serverless compute so parties work together without direct access to each other's data; notebooks are reviewed and run by named collaborators and results go to an output catalog; collaborators are identified by Unity Catalog metastore identifiers.

Lakehouse Federation queries external sources in place through a connection and a foreign catalog, described as read-only; pushdown is partial and shown by EXPLAIN FORMATTED; fetchSize sets rows per batch, not parallelism.

UniForm generates Iceberg metadata asynchronously for a Delta table's Parquet files, records converted_delta_version, requires column mapping and is read-only for Iceberg clients; Iceberg REST catalogs can vend short-lived storage credentials, and Unity Catalog issues them only with external access enabled and EXTERNAL USE SCHEMA granted.
Lakeflow Connect ingests sources into Databricks through connector categories including change-data-capture database ingestion, files, streaming and query-based ingestion.

Databricks' current documentation calls its sharing product family OpenSharing and the historical delta-sharing URL leads to the OpenSharing overview; the open protocol is specified as the Delta Sharing Protocol, and connectors and APIs keep identifiers such as deltaSharing, delta_sharing, shares and recipients.

Delta Sharing reads are bearer-token REST calls answered with short-lived file URLs or temporary credentials that the client uses to download from the provider's storage; hints are best effort; history sharing gates older versions; a profile file without expirationTime has a token that never expires.

Databricks-to-Databricks recipients use a sharing identifier and no token; open recipients use a credential file downloaded once or OIDC federation; rotate_token only shortens the old token and 0 ends it at once; the share owner must keep SELECT on shared tables; recipient revocation needs no extra privilege.

Adaptive query execution re-plans at query-stage boundaries from runtime statistics: it coalesces post-shuffle partitions and converts a sort-merge join to a broadcast hash join when the runtime statistics of any join side fall below the threshold, which is less efficient than planning the broadcast in the first place but avoids sorting and can read shuffle files locally.

Join strategy hints such as BROADCAST instruct the planner; spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold (default 10 MB, -1 disables) sets the size below which Spark broadcasts a relation automatically when it knows the size.

DataFrame.cache persists at the MEMORY_AND_DISK_DESER storage level; persisted data is stored the first time an action computes it; Spark SQL caches tables for reuse and unpersist or uncacheTable removes them.
A driver program's SparkContext coordinates executor processes that run tasks and store data; the driver schedules its own tasks and sends them to executors.
Databricks Runtime applies many optimizations automatically, including disk caching for Parquet reads, dynamic file pruning and adaptive query execution.
DataFrame.explain prints logical and physical plans; formatted mode prints an outline plus node details, and the other modes are simple, extended, codegen and cost.
Transformations are lazy and build a plan; actions such as collect() start the computation and return values to the driver.
spark.driver.maxResultSize caps the total serialized result bytes an action may return to the driver and aborts the job when exceeded; its documented default is 1g.

A shuffle re-distributes data so it is grouped differently across partitions, copying rows across executors, and is a costly operation; collect() fetches an entire dataset to one machine and can make the driver run out of memory.

spark.sql.shuffle.partitions (default 200) sets the partitions used when shuffling data for joins or aggregations; adaptive coalescing then merges small post-shuffle partitions toward an advisory size (64 MB) while respecting a minimum partition size (1 MB) when parallelism comes first.

Adaptive skew-join handling treats a partition as skewed only when it exceeds skewedPartitionFactor (default 5) times the median partition size and skewedPartitionThresholdInBytes (default 256 MB), and then splits, and if needed replicates, the skewed tasks of sort-merge and shuffle hash joins.

A task-level out-of-memory error can come from one task's working set being too large; raising the level of parallelism makes each task's input smaller and is the simplest documented fix; short tasks are cheap to launch.
The Stages tab lists per-stage shuffle read and write in bytes and records and summarizes task metrics, including shuffle spill.

A driver program coordinates executors that run tasks; transformations build a lazy plan and actions execute it; a shuffle redistributes rows across partitions and is costly; explain() prints the plan in several modes; collect() returns all rows to the driver.

collect() fetches the entire dataset to the driver and can make it run out of memory; spark.driver.maxResultSize (default 1g) aborts an action whose serialized results exceed it; DataFrame.cache() persists with the MEMORY_AND_DISK_DESER storage level.
The Stages tab of the Spark web UI shows each stage's shuffle read and write in bytes and records and summarizes task metrics, including duration and shuffle spill.

Spark SQL can cache tables and DataFrames; join strategy hints such as BROADCAST steer the planner; adaptive query execution uses runtime statistics to coalesce post-shuffle partitions, convert a sort-merge join to a broadcast join when any side is below the threshold at runtime, and split a join partition that exceeds both a factor of the median partition size and a byte threshold.
SQL Server Agent runs jobs on recurring or one-time schedules, at Agent start, on CPU idle or on demand, on the server's clock.
Spark 4.0 enables ANSI mode by default, raising errors for invalid operations instead of returning NULL.

The Lakeflow Connect SQL Server connector ingests incrementally using change tracking or change data capture, recommends change tracking for tables with a primary key, and supports on-premises SQL Server over private network connections.
SQL Server DATETIME rounds fractional seconds to .000, .003 or .007 and stores no time zone offset.
Databricks UTF8_LCASE collation compares strings case-insensitively after lower-casing, keeps accents distinct and is recommended for migrations from simple case-insensitive systems.
SQL Server DECIMAL and NUMERIC are exact fixed-precision types with precision up to 38 and a declared scale.
In T-SQL, integer divided by integer truncates the fractional part; Databricks div returns the integral part as BIGINT.

SQL Server IDENTITY values may have gaps after restarts and are not guaranteed consecutive; Delta identity columns are BIGINT only, unique but not necessarily consecutive, and disable concurrent transactions on the table.

SQL Server READ COMMITTED uses locking unless READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT is ON, when it uses row versioning; Delta tables default to WriteSerializable isolation, under which concurrent DELETE, UPDATE or MERGE operations can conflict.
Lakeflow Jobs run one or many tasks with dependencies and run-if conditions such as all succeeded and at least one failed, started by schedule or event triggers such as file arrival.
Lakebridge is a Databricks Labs toolkit that analyzes source metadata and dependencies, transpiles SQL and reconciles source and target data.

Restarting from the same checkpoint does not allow changing the number or type of input sources, nor any change to the schema of a stateful operation such as grouping keys or aggregates, because state is restored with the schema it was written with.
With a checkpoint location a query records the offset range of each trigger in write-ahead logs and saves running aggregates, so after a failure or an intentional stop it continues where it left off.

Watermark-based state cleanup needs append or update output mode, an aggregation on the event-time column or on a window of it, and withWatermark on that same column before the aggregation; complete mode keeps all aggregation state.
On Databricks a checkpoint records a query's offsets, commits and state; deleting or changing its location starts the query fresh, and each query needs its own checkpoint location.

Databricks documents foreachBatch as receiving each micro-batch's output with its batch identity, leaves duplicate writes and failure handling to the sink logic, and requires stateful queries to consume each batch DataFrame completely.

Streaming deduplication on a unique identifier keeps past identifiers as state; adding a watermark and the event-time column lets old state be removed, and dropDuplicatesWithinWatermark deduplicates within the watermark delay when event time cannot be part of the identifier.

Event time is the time embedded in the data rather than when Spark receives it; a window aggregation is a grouping on the event-time column in which each window is a group and one row can belong to several windows.

End-to-end exactly-once needs a replayable source, the checkpointed engine and an idempotent sink; the file sink is exactly-once, the Kafka and foreach sinks are at-least-once, and foreachBatch depends on the function: at-least-once by default, exactly-once only if it uses the batch id or another key to deduplicate, with the semantics of any extra operations it applies left to the user.

The file source processes new files in modification-time order, expects each file to appear atomically (for example by a move), limits new files per micro-batch with maxFilesPerTrigger, requires a user-specified schema by default, and is fault-tolerant.
A watermark delay guarantees that data less late than the delay is never dropped; data later than the delay is not guaranteed to be dropped and may or may not be aggregated.

A stream-static join keeps no state; a stream-stream join buffers past rows of both inputs as state, which watermarks plus an event-time constraint bound; outer and semi joins must declare them, and outer NULL rows arrive only after the delay and time range have passed.

Structured Streaming treats a stream as an input table that keeps being appended; Spark runs the query incrementally, reading only new data, keeping only the intermediate state needed, and by default executing a series of small batch jobs called micro-batches.

Append writes only result rows that will never change, which for an aggregation requires a watermark and delays each window by the threshold; update writes rows changed since the last trigger; complete rewrites the whole result table; an aggregation without a watermark cannot use append.

When a query unions or joins several streams, Spark tracks each stream's maximum event time and applies one global watermark, the minimum by default; the max policy follows the fastest stream and drops slower streams' data more aggressively.

Since Spark 3.2 a RocksDB state store provider keeps state in native memory and on local disk instead of the executor JVM heap, to avoid long garbage-collection pauses with millions of state keys, with the same checkpoint-based fault tolerance.
session_window builds windows of dynamic length: a session starts with an input, extends while further inputs arrive within the gap duration, and closes when no input arrives for the gap.

The state store is a versioned key-value store that carries stateful operators across micro-batches; the default provider keeps state in executor JVM memory backed by checkpoint files, and the experimental state data source reads that state back from a checkpoint.

With no trigger a micro-batch starts when the previous one ends; a fixed interval skips intervals without new data; the deprecated one-time trigger gives way to availableNow, which processes everything available at the start in one or more micro-batches, finishes uncommitted batches first, advances the watermark per batch, runs a final no-data batch when that moved the watermark, and stops; continuous processing is experimental and at-least-once.

withWatermark(column, threshold) lets the engine keep a window's state, and let late data update it, until the maximum event time seen minus the threshold passes the window's end; in append mode the window's final result is written only then, after which its state is dropped.

Tumbling windows are fixed, non-overlapping and hold each input once; sliding windows are fixed but overlap when the slide is shorter than the window, so an input can fall in several; session windows grow while inputs keep arriving within a gap.
A watermark delay guarantees that data less late than the delay is never dropped; data later than the delay may or may not be aggregated.
Stream-static joins are not stateful; stream-stream joins buffer both inputs as state, bounded by watermarks and an event-time constraint that outer and semi joins must declare.

Structured Streaming runs a query incrementally over an input table that keeps being appended, by default as micro-batches whose timing a trigger sets; availableNow processes the data present at the start in one or more micro-batches and stops, and file-based sources need a user-specified schema by default.

A checkpoint records each trigger's offset range in write-ahead logs together with state and commits, so a query resumes where it left off; changing the number or type of sources or a stateful operation's schema between restarts is not allowed, and a new checkpoint location starts the query fresh.

End-to-end exactly-once needs replayable sources and idempotent sinks; the file sink is exactly-once, Kafka and foreach sinks are at-least-once, and foreachBatch is at-least-once by default and exactly-once only when it deduplicates, for example by batch id.

Event time is the time in the data; window aggregations group on it, sliding windows can hold an event more than once, and a watermark (latest event time minus a threshold) lets the engine finalize a window and drop its state once it passes the window's end; output modes decide which result rows reach the sink.

MCP servers expose tools, resources and prompts to hosts over standard transports: stdio for a local subprocess and Streamable HTTP for a server at a URL, with SSE also supported by the Python SDK; protocol revisions are dated.
